# Configuration reference

<!-- Code generated by chok docs gen from the Config types; DO NOT EDIT. -->

Every key an application built on chok v3 can set, read from the
configuration types: `chok.Base`, which every application's Config embeds,
and the Config of `db` and of each battery. An application names a
battery's section in its own Config struct; the keys below carry the
names examples/blog and `chok init` use: `db`, `auth` for identity, `jobs`,
`telemetry`, `cache`, `realtime` and `mail`.

`chok.Load` reads, lowest to highest: the defaults below, the file
(`chok.yaml`, `<name>.yaml`, `configs/<name>.yaml` or `--config`), environment
variables and flags. A key's variable is the application's prefix and
the key's path in upper case, dots and dashes as underscores:
`http.addr` is `<NAME>_HTTP_ADDR`; a list is comma-separated. `[]` marks
the fields of a list's elements and `<name>` a map entry, both set in
the file. A misspelled key fails startup with a suggestion, and
`--check-config` prints the configuration in effect.

**Rules** are the `validate` tags, checked when the configuration loads;
Validate methods add the checks between keys that the descriptions
mention. A **secret** is masked wherever the configuration is printed:
set it through the environment, not in the file.

Embedded without a tag in every application's Config, so its sections `app`, `http` and `log` sit at the top level.

| `app.shutdown_timeout` | duration | `30s` |  | ShutdownTimeout bounds the whole stop phase: drain, HTTP shutdown, stopping the Starters and closing every component. |
| `app.start_timeout` | duration | `30s` |  | StartTimeout bounds the start phase: every Healther must report healthy within it before the HTTP server listens. |
| `http.addr` | string | `:8080` |  |  |

| `http.cors.allow_headers` | list of string | `Origin,Content-Type,Accept,Authorization,X-Request-Id` |  |  |
| `http.cors.allow_methods` | list of string | `GET,POST,PUT,PATCH,DELETE,HEAD,OPTIONS` |  |  |
| `http.cors.allow_origins` | list of string |  |  | AllowOrigins lists the allowed origins; "\*" allows any. |

## `identity.Config` — section `auth`

Accounts, tokens, OAuth providers and the audit log; `identity.New` takes it. The provider entries are keyed by name, such as `google`.

| Key | Type | Default | Rules | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `auth.allowed_redirect_backs` | list of string |  |  | AllowedRedirectBacks lists the absolute URLs an OAuth sign-in may return to through ?redirect_back: an entry ending in / allows its subtree, any other entry that page. Relative paths are always allowed. |
| `auth.audit.admin_api` | bool | `true` |  | AdminAPI mounts GET /audit/logs for administrators: the principal needs the admin role, or the audit/read permission once identity/rbac is in use. |
| `auth.audit.async_buffer` | int | `1024` |  | AsyncBuffer is how many records Log queues for the writer. |
| `auth.audit.drop_on_full` | bool |  |  | DropOnFull drops a record when the queue is full, instead of making Log wait for room (or for the caller's context to end). |
| `auth.audit.enabled` | bool |  |  | Enabled turns the audit log on; off, Log does nothing. |
| `auth.audit.retention` | duration | `4320h` |  | Retention is how long a record is kept; older ones are purged every hour. 0 keeps records forever. |
| `auth.disable_register` | bool |  |  | DisableRegister drops the register route: accounts come from Users().Create. |
| `auth.link_by_email` | bool |  |  | LinkByEmail lets a first OAuth sign-in join the local account with the same email, when that account's email is verified and the provider vouches for the address and does not alias it. |
| `auth.login_rate_limit` | int | `10` |  | LoginRateWindow and LoginRateLimit throttle failed logins: once an email, or a client IP, has failed LoginRateLimit times within the window, login answers 429 until the window slides. Both 0 turn the throttle off. |
| `auth.login_rate_window` | duration | `15m` |  | LoginRateWindow and LoginRateLimit throttle failed logins: once an email, or a client IP, has failed LoginRateLimit times within the window, login answers 429 until the window slides. Both 0 turn the throttle off. |
| `auth.oauth_callback_frontend_url` | string |  |  | OAuthCallbackFrontendURL is the front-end page an OAuth callback sends the browser to with a one-time ?code, which the page trades for a token at {prefix}/exchange. Required with providers. |
| `auth.prefix` | string | `/auth` |  | Prefix is where the routes mount: {prefix}/register, {prefix}/login, ... |
| `auth.providers.<name>.client_id` | string |  |  | ClientID is the OAuth client: Google's client ID, GitHub's and Facebook's app ID, Apple's Services ID. |
| `auth.providers.<name>.client_secret` | string |  | **secret** | ClientSecret is the client's secret; for Apple, the PEM contents of the .p8 signing key. |
| `auth.providers.<name>.endpoint` | string |  |  | Endpoint replaces the provider's base URL: a GitHub Enterprise server, a Graph API version for Facebook, the issuer for Google and Apple (a test server, mostly). |
| `auth.providers.<name>.hosted_domain` | string |  |  | HostedDomain accepts only accounts of one Google Workspace domain. |
| `auth.providers.<name>.key_id` | string |  |  | TeamID and KeyID identify Apple's signing key: the developer team and the key, ten characters each. |
| `auth.providers.<name>.redirect_url` | string |  |  | RedirectURL is the callback registered with the provider: https://api.example.com/auth/google/callback. |
| `auth.providers.<name>.scopes` | list of string |  |  | Scopes replaces the provider's default scopes. |
| `auth.providers.<name>.team_id` | string |  |  | TeamID and KeyID identify Apple's signing key: the developer team and the key, ten characters each. |
| `auth.refresh_ttl` | duration | `168h` |  | RefreshTTL bounds a session: refresh-token issues fresh tokens until RefreshTTL after the login that started the session, then the user logs in again. Every session ends: 0 takes the default. |
| `auth.reset_ttl` | duration | `15m` |  | ResetTTL is how long a password-reset token is valid. |
| `auth.reset_url` | string |  |  | ResetURL is the front end's password-reset page, an absolute URL: given, the password-reset Mail's Link is ResetURL?token=&lt;token&gt;, for the page to post to {prefix}/reset-password; without it the application builds the link from Mail.Token. |
| `auth.signing_key` | string |  | **secret** | SigningKey signs the access and password-reset tokens (HS256); at least 32 bytes. |
| `auth.token_ttl` | duration | `2h` |  | TokenTTL is how long an access token is valid. |

## `jobs.Config` — section `jobs`

Periodic jobs and transactional-outbox workers; `jobs.New` takes it.

| Key | Type | Default | Rules | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jobs.batch_size` | int | `100` |  | BatchSize is how many messages a sweep reads per query, and how many the cleanup deletes per statement; a sweep reads at most 100 batches, the rest wait for the next one. At most 10000. |
| `jobs.cleanup_interval` | duration | `1h` |  | CleanupInterval is how often the retention cleanup runs. |
| `jobs.enabled` | bool | `true` |  | Enabled runs the periodic jobs and the workers in this process. False makes an enqueue-only process: Enqueue works, nothing runs. Run the workers in one process (one replica) of a deployment. |
| `jobs.poll_interval` | duration | `1s` |  | PollInterval is how often each worker sweeps its topic for new messages: the delivery latency while it keeps up. |
| `jobs.retention` | duration |  |  | Retention deletes, every CleanupInterval, the messages older than Retention that every worker has delivered; 0 keeps them forever. The cleanup goes by the watermarks of the workers of its own process: one without workers deletes nothing. |
| `jobs.settle_window` | duration | `30s` |  | SettleWindow bounds how long a transaction that calls Enqueue may take to commit: a worker's watermark never passes messages younger than this, so a late commit is still delivered. Raise it if enqueueing transactions run longer, and keep the clocks of the processes that enqueue in sync. |
| `jobs.stop_budget` | duration | `15s` |  | StopBudget is how long stopping waits for runs in flight, after telling them to stop through their context. |

## `telemetry.Config` — section `telemetry`

Prometheus metrics, OpenTelemetry traces and the slog bridge to OpenTelemetry logs; `telemetry.New` takes it.

| Key | Type | Default | Rules | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `telemetry.logs.otel` | bool |  |  | OTel copies every record the App's loggers write (those New builds from the log section, the access log included) to OpenTelemetry Logs, exported over OTLP to Tracing.Endpoint with the trace and span id of the request; the log output itself is unchanged. |
| `telemetry.metrics.enabled` | bool | `true` |  | Enabled records the HTTP and database metrics, with the Go runtime and process collectors, and serves them on Path in the Prometheus text format. Off, the registry stays empty. |
| `telemetry.metrics.path` | string | `/metrics` |  | Path is where the App serves the metrics. |
| `telemetry.tracing.enabled` | bool |  |  | Enabled records a span for every request and, through Instrument, every SQL statement, and exports them. |
| `telemetry.tracing.endpoint` | string | `http://localhost:4318` |  | Endpoint is the OpenTelemetry collector's base URL, as in OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT: spans are posted to &lt;endpoint&gt;/v1/traces and, with Logs.OTel, log records to &lt;endpoint&gt;/v1/logs. https uses TLS with the system roots. The other OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_\* variables (headers, certificates, timeout) still apply. |
| `telemetry.tracing.exporter` | string | `stdout` | `oneof=stdout otlp` | Exporter is where spans go: stdout (one JSON object per span, for development) or otlp (OTLP over HTTP to Endpoint). |
| `telemetry.tracing.sample_ratio` | float64 | `1` |  | SampleRatio is the fraction of new traces recorded, in (0, 1]; a request whose traceparent says sampled is always recorded. |
| `telemetry.tracing.service_name` | string |  |  | ServiceName is the service.name of the spans and log records; empty takes OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, else the executable's name. |

## `cache.Config` — section `cache`

The in-memory and Redis cache layers and the circuit breaker in front of Redis; `cache.New` takes it.

| Key | Type | Default | Rules | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cache.breaker.enabled` | bool |  |  | Enabled puts a circuit breaker in front of Redis: after Threshold failures in a row Redis is left alone for ResetTimeout, its reads are misses and its writes are skipped; then one probe at a time goes through, and HalfOpenSuccesses successes in a row close the breaker again. A Redis that is down then costs a miss instead of a timeout per call, and the Cache reports healthy: the application serves from its database meanwhile. |
| `cache.breaker.half_open_successes` | int | `3` |  | Enabled puts a circuit breaker in front of Redis: after Threshold failures in a row Redis is left alone for ResetTimeout, its reads are misses and its writes are skipped; then one probe at a time goes through, and HalfOpenSuccesses successes in a row close the breaker again. A Redis that is down then costs a miss instead of a timeout per call, and the Cache reports healthy: the application serves from its database meanwhile. |
| `cache.breaker.probe_timeout` | duration | `2s` |  | ProbeTimeout bounds a probe on its own, so a caller's nearly spent deadline cannot fail it; it is at most ResetTimeout. |
| `cache.breaker.reset_timeout` | duration | `30s` |  | Enabled puts a circuit breaker in front of Redis: after Threshold failures in a row Redis is left alone for ResetTimeout, its reads are misses and its writes are skipped; then one probe at a time goes through, and HalfOpenSuccesses successes in a row close the breaker again. A Redis that is down then costs a miss instead of a timeout per call, and the Cache reports healthy: the application serves from its database meanwhile. |
| `cache.breaker.threshold` | int | `5` |  | Enabled puts a circuit breaker in front of Redis: after Threshold failures in a row Redis is left alone for ResetTimeout, its reads are misses and its writes are skipped; then one probe at a time goes through, and HalfOpenSuccesses successes in a row close the breaker again. A Redis that is down then costs a miss instead of a timeout per call, and the Cache reports healthy: the application serves from its database meanwhile. |
| `cache.memory.capacity` | int | `10000` |  | Capacity is the most entries kept; the least likely to be used again go first. |
| `cache.memory.enabled` | bool |  |  | Enabled keeps entries in this process. Each replica has its own: a Delete reaches this replica's memory and Redis, not the other replicas' memory, so keep TTL short for data that changes. |
| `cache.memory.ttl` | duration | `5m` |  | TTL is how long an entry lives when Set is given no TTL. |
| `cache.redis.addr` | string | `127.0.0.1:6379` |  |  |
| `cache.redis.ca_cert` | string |  |  | TLS encrypts the connection, verifying the server against the system roots, or against CACert when it is set (CACert alone turns TLS on), as managed Redis services require. |
| `cache.redis.db` | int |  |  |  |
| `cache.redis.dial_timeout` | duration | `1s` |  | The timeouts are short on purpose: a cache that answers late is worse than a miss. |
| `cache.redis.enabled` | bool |  |  | Enabled keeps entries in Redis, shared by every replica. |
| `cache.redis.password` | string |  | **secret** |  |
| `cache.redis.pool_size` | int | `10` |  |  |
| `cache.redis.read_timeout` | duration | `500ms` |  |  |
| `cache.redis.tls` | bool |  |  | TLS encrypts the connection, verifying the server against the system roots, or against CACert when it is set (CACert alone turns TLS on), as managed Redis services require. |
| `cache.redis.ttl` | duration | `10m` |  | TTL is how long an entry lives when Set is given no TTL. |
| `cache.redis.username` | string |  |  | a Redis 6 ACL user; empty is the default user |
| `cache.redis.write_timeout` | duration | `500ms` |  |  |

## `realtime.Config` — section `realtime`

The hub that pushes events to browsers over WebSocket and server-sent events, its one-time tickets and its Redis backplane; `realtime.New` takes it.

| Key | Type | Default | Rules | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `realtime.allowed_origins` | list of string |  |  | AllowedOrigins admits browser WebSockets from these origins besides the server's own host: host patterns in path.Match syntax, such as app.example.com or \*.example.com, matched against the Origin's host (against scheme://host when a pattern has a scheme); "\*" admits any origin. Empty admits the same host only. Server-sent event streams are ordinary requests that CORS governs. |
| `realtime.channel` | string | `chok:realtime` |  | Channel is the Redis channel of the backplane and the prefix of the tickets' keys; deployments sharing one Redis each need their own. |
| `realtime.max_subscriptions` | int | `64` |  | MaxSubscriptions caps the topics of one connection: beyond it a WebSocket is closed with 1008 and a stream request answers 400. |
| `realtime.path` | string | `/realtime` |  | Path prefixes the three endpoints: {Path}/ticket, {Path}/ws and {Path}/sse. It starts with a slash and does not end with one. |
| `realtime.ping_interval` | duration | `25s` |  | PingInterval paces the heartbeats: a WebSocket ping, which the client must answer within two intervals or be disconnected, and an SSE comment line. |
| `realtime.replay` | int | `256` |  | Replay is how many recent events the hub keeps, across all topics, for clients that resume after an event they saw; 0 turns resuming off, so every resume gets a reset event. |
| `realtime.send_buffer` | int | `64` |  | SendBuffer is how many published events may wait for one connection. A connection that falls further behind is a slow consumer: the hub drops it (a WebSocket with close code 4408) and counts it in Stats.Dropped. What a subscription adds — the events it replays, its refused or reset events — does not count, but nothing waits beyond SendBuffer + Replay + 2 × MaxSubscriptions events. |
| `realtime.ticket_ttl` | duration | `60s` |  | TicketTTL is how long a ticket from {Path}/ticket can be redeemed. |

## `mail.Config` — section `mail`

Transactional mail through an SMTP relay, into .eml files or into the log; `mail.New` takes it.

| Key | Type | Default | Rules | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mail.dir` | string |  |  | Dir is where transport dir writes, one {unix nanoseconds}-{random}.eml file per mail; required with it, and created by New. |
| `mail.from` | string |  |  | From is the sender, "Name &lt;addr&gt;" or "addr"; required. Message-IDs take its domain. |
| `mail.reply_to` | string |  |  | ReplyTo is where replies go, when not to From. |
| `mail.smtp.host` | string |  |  | Host is the relay; required with transport smtp. |
| `mail.smtp.password` | string |  | **secret** | Username and Password authenticate with AUTH PLAIN, over TLS only (or to a loopback host); an empty Username skips authentication. |
| `mail.smtp.port` | int | `587` |  | Port is the relay's port: 587 with starttls, 465 with implicit. |
| `mail.smtp.tls` | string | `starttls` | `omitempty,oneof=starttls implicit none` | TLS is starttls (upgrade the plain connection; the relay must offer it), implicit (TLS from the first byte) or none, which only a loopback host may use, for local debugging. |
| `mail.smtp.username` | string |  |  | Username and Password authenticate with AUTH PLAIN, over TLS only (or to a loopback host); an empty Username skips authentication. |
| `mail.timeout` | duration | `15s` |  | Timeout bounds one Send: dialing, TLS, authentication and delivery. |
| `mail.transport` | string | `smtp` | `omitempty,oneof=smtp dir log` | Transport is how a mail leaves: smtp sends it; dir writes it as an .eml file into Dir, for development, examples and tests; log only logs it. A Sender option replaces the transport, and then Transport and its settings are ignored. |
